# Blocks, Proof of Work and Difficulty

Miners assemble valid transactions into candidate blocks and search for a
header whose proof-of-work hash satisfies the current target. RinHash combines
BLAKE3, Argon2d, and SHA3-256. Its memory-hard stage is intended to increase the
cost of fixed-function specialisation compared with simple hash-only
proof-of-work designs. Specialisation resistance is parameter-dependent and is
not a permanent guarantee of equal CPU, GPU, FPGA, or ASIC economics
[@rincoinCore2026deployed].

Rincoin targets one block every 60 seconds. Dark Gravity Wave v3 adjusts
difficulty from recent block history so that the network can respond to changes
in available hashrate. Difficulty adjustment governs the work required for a
valid block; it does not alter the subsidy schedule
[@rincoinCore2026deployed].

Nodes choose among valid histories by cumulative proof of work. A chain with
more blocks is not necessarily preferred if it represents less accumulated
work.
